schoolsPage.heading: Navigating Schools
schoolsPage.intro: We've heard from therapists that navigating schools is one of the most complex and challenging parts of this job. Based on therapist input, we've put together tips for working with schools, plus practical tools to keep key school information handy over the course of treatment.

quote.text: We're definitely navigating 50 systems every time we walk into a school.

tips.title: Find and connect with a school partner
tips.body: When a youth requests for sessions to occur in the school through Rise, the Rise therapist reaches out to the QRS (qualified referral source): the person who entered the referral. This is often the Mental Health Advocate, School Counselor, Interventionist, or School Social Worker. This person can help determine the best time to meet with the youth based on their school schedule, and where sessions can be held. The Rise therapist is expected to communicate with the QRS at least 24 hours before coming to the school to meet with the youth.

tips.title: Connect with your school partner and answer key questions
tips.body: Use the interview guide below to get your important questions about working in the school answered. The goal is to equip you with what you need to understand the specific school context and work effectively there. Each time you start working in a new school, find a school contact for a brief meeting or phone call to go through these questions. Your answers save in this browser and carry over to Your Client's School Card.

tips.title: Clarify the roles of school personnel, the Rise therapist, and Rise admin
tips.body: Youth and families may be confused about the roles of the school and their therapist, and may or may not know about the role of Rise admin. Give young people clear information about roles and confidentiality. You can open the discussion by asking whether they've heard of confidentiality before and exploring what they think it means. Validate that it can be hard to keep track of all the adults involved in their care, and provide psychoeducation about each role.

tips.title: Get a Release of Information to communicate with the youth's school
tips.body: We strongly suggest getting a signed release of information (ROI) form from the youth and family so you can exchange information with the client's school.

tips.title: Learn the school's policies and practices
tips.body: We are developing a set of policies, practices, and insider tips for working in the schools we serve. More soon!

tips.title: Be prepared to support youth through school re-entry after a crisis
tips.body: Youth with suicidal thoughts and behaviors often move in and out of schools and other systems of care. A supported return to school helps protect the progress made in reducing suicidal thoughts and behaviors, so be prepared to support youth through these transitions.
tips.linkText: Open the school re-entry resource guide

interviewGuide.heading: School partner interview guide
interviewGuide.printHint: Prints the questions with any answers you've added, plus space to write, so you can bring it to the meeting.
questions: Where can I meet with clients in your school?
What are the best and worst times to meet with clients?
What do I need to know about re-integrating youth into school?
Is there a re-entry meeting? Who attends?
What are the school-based risk assessment procedures?
What happens during a school emergency or lockdown?
What else should I know about working with your school?
What other mental health resources are available in the school?
Who helps connect families with resources in your school?

roles.role: Facilitates and funds therapy, and supports linkage to follow-up treatment when needed.
Links the youth with a therapist. Sometimes the school also provides space and scheduling support for Rise therapy sessions.
Provides therapy to the youth, assesses outcomes (including changes in suicidal thoughts and behaviors), and links to follow-up care.

rolesPicker.label: Who handles this?
rolesPicker.intro: Pick a situation to see whose role it is. You can walk through this with youth and families too.

options.label: Getting connected with a therapist
options.note: The school links the youth with a therapist. The school partner (QRS) enters the referral to Rise.

options.label: Finding a time and place to meet at school
options.note: The school partner (QRS) helps with scheduling around the youth's classes and finding a private space. Give them at least 24 hours' notice.

options.label: Paying for therapy
options.note: Rise funds therapy, so there is no cost to the youth or family.

options.label: What happens in sessions, and what stays private
options.note: The therapist provides therapy and explains confidentiality: what stays between them, and when information has to be shared to keep the youth safe.

options.label: Checking whether things are getting better
options.note: The therapist assesses outcomes, including changes in suicidal thoughts and behaviors, through screenings during treatment.

options.label: Next steps in care after Rise
options.note: The therapist links the youth to follow-up care, and Rise supports that linkage when needed.

guidelines.heading: Rise School Guidelines
guidelines.intro: When seeing Rise clients in the school setting, the Rise provider is a representative of Rise Against Suicide. Follow the school's policies and procedures, as well as the Rise protocol below.
items: The QRS is the only school staff member the Rise provider communicates with at the school. Never reach out to the principal or a school administrator unless directed to by the QRS.
Rise providers do not speak on behalf of Rise in the school setting unless Rise staff are present or have arranged it.
Regular communication between the Rise provider and the QRS is encouraged while the client is progressing through sessions.
For a Rise provider to see a youth, the Rise referral process must be completed in the Rise RMS or through a Rise staff member.
If the client has a social service need, the school counselor or appropriate school staff may be notified to help the student.
Give the QRS at least 24 hours' notice before arriving to see a client at the school, including arranging a place to meet the student.
Sign in at the front desk and ask for the QRS who contacted you.
Immediately report any concerns about the young person to the QRS, and collaborate on school policies and procedures.
Respond within 24 hours on business days to QRS outreach about availability and fit.
Rise providers are not available to school staff for consultation services as part of the Rise program.
